set.typical_award_size: Concord is a CDBG entitlement city. Its FY 2026/27 Action Plan (Expected Resources table) shows a CDBG annual allocation of $967,306 plus $23,392 program income and $214,094 prior-year resources, $1,204,792 total, and about $1,000,000 a year expected over the 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan; the City also has a small housing rehabilitation revolving loan fund and $88,200 of Cannabis Community Benefit Funds (non-housing). Concord's HOME share is pooled in the County-administered Contra Costa HOME Consortium (Antioch, Concord, Pittsburg, Walnut Creek and the Urban County). The Consortium released the FY 2027/28 CDBG and ESG RFP/NOFA on October 15, 2026 through City Data Services for a three-year cycle FY 2027/28 through 2029/30 (Concord awards are for FY 2027/28 with possible renewal through FY 2030); one joint application serves all five jurisdictions. Concord uses CDBG for public services, homeowner rehabilitation (including Habitat for Humanity's rehabilitation program), fair housing and public facilities, and requires a 20% match on CDBG projects; housing development is funded from the City's own funds.
set.layering_notes: For multifamily development, treat Concord CDBG as minor (rehab, fair housing and public facility set-asides) and apply to the County for HOME and Measure X (county record: Contra Costa County Affordable Housing Program: HOME and CDBG-Housing). Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-assisted projects of 8 or more units and HOME projects of 12 or more. set.typical_award_size: Richmond does not run its own CDBG or HOME program. The adopted Housing Element states that although Richmond is eligible to be a HUD entitlement city, after staffing cuts the City opted for Contra Costa County to receive its share of HUD funding, and that the County administers CDBG and HOME for Richmond; the County CDBG page defines the Urban County as the entire county less Antioch, Concord, Pittsburg and Walnut Creek, so Richmond is inside the Urban County and the County HOME Consortium. The Housing Element cites the CDBG-assisted rehabilitation of the 150-unit Hacienda Apartments. The Richmond Housing Authority no longer administers vouchers: the County administers the Housing Choice Voucher program (about 1,700 vouchers used in Richmond, including project-based vouchers), and Miraflores received 79 RHA project-based vouchers earlier. The 2015 HUD figure of $1,092,323 predates the switch and should not be used.
set.affordability_requirement: CDBG national objective (80% AMI); HOME rent limits and County regulatory agreements (55 years on County-funded rental projects); HACCC PBV requirements for voucher-assisted units.
